title: Regulatory inventory, applicability determinations and Echelon's own regulatory status
status_rationale: Unbound requires a machine-checkable applicability register with citation, jurisdiction, affected entity, classification and accountable reviewer (UNB-REGMAP-001), explicit recording of inapplicable, disputed, guidance-only and proposed obligations (UNB-REGMAP-003), re-evaluation triggers (UNB-REGMAP-004), and an OperatorStatusRegister mapping features to licensing questions such as investment adviser or money transmitter status (UNB-XIN-REG-002). Design choices intended to keep Unbound outside licensed roles are recorded (CNV-LEG-001: no holding of funds, no payment execution, no individualized investment advice; CNV-PAY-001: Unbound as Nacha third-party service provider, sponsor as originator). Agents cannot publish legal interpretations as binding policy (AIN-035, GOV-AUTH-011). Nothing is implemented and no counsel review is recorded.
target_answer: Echelon maintains one regulatory applicability register covering law that binds Echelon itself (for example OFAC, FTC Safeguards Rule if applicable, state privacy and breach laws, California charitable fundraising platform registration per CNV-LEG-002), law that binds customers and flows to Echelon by contract or supervisory expectation (GLBA, Interagency TPRM guidance, BSCA, Nacha, IRC DAF provisions, SEC and FINRA recordkeeping), and guidance or proposals (marked as such). Each row has primary citation, classification, affected entity, facts relied on, counsel reviewer and date, and mapped controls. Echelon's own status (not a money transmitter, not an investment adviser, Nacha TPSP) is a recorded counsel determination tied to funds-flow conformance checks that block deployments that would change it. AI may draft analyses but only counsel-approved interpretations become binding.
intended_practice: Build the register per UNB-REGMAP-001 to 006 and obtain counsel review of operator status before any customer deployment.
customer_statement: Echelon has designed a regulatory applicability register and a product architecture intended to avoid holding funds, executing payments or giving investment advice. The register is not built and Echelon's regulatory status has not yet been confirmed by counsel.
open_questions: Has counsel reviewed whether any planned Unbound feature would require money transmitter, investment adviser or broker registration?

title: Compliance monitoring and testing against mapped obligations
status_rationale: UNB-REGMAP-002 requires a reviewer-approved many-to-many mapping from obligation to control to test to evidence and blocks the compliance gate for binding obligations without an independently verified control. SOC2-019 distinguishes control states and SOC2-024 requires owner attestation and independent challenge. Not implemented; the master control matrix shows all controls Designed with no operating evidence, test execution or auditor review.
target_answer: Every binding obligation in the register maps to controls, tests and evidence. Compliance status is computed from evidence, not declared: a control without current evidence shows as failing. Compliance issues are tracked with owner, severity, due date and escalation, and an independent compliance review tests the program annually. The deployment gate refuses activation for a customer when an applicable binding obligation lacks a verified control.
intended_practice: Implement per UNB-REGMAP-002 and the continuous control monitoring architecture.
customer_statement: Echelon plans compliance monitoring in which each applicable obligation is mapped to controls, tests and evidence, with status computed from evidence. Not yet implemented.

title: Regulator examination access (Bank Service Company Act) and cooperation with customer examinations
status_rationale: No contract terms or procedures exist. Unbound provides for auditor-ready Folio evidence packages (SOC2-009), replayable decisions (GOV-AUTH-022) and partner isolation of audit evidence (GOV-AUTH-016), which would support examinations but are not built. Echelon has never been examined.
target_answer: Echelon contractually acknowledges that, when it performs services for an insured depository institution, those services are subject to examination by the institution's federal banking regulator to the same extent as if performed by the institution (12 U.S.C. 1867(c)), and supports the institution's notice of the service relationship to its regulator. Echelon commits to cooperate with examinations of its customers by any regulator with jurisdiction (federal banking agencies, SEC, FINRA, state regulators, IRS), to provide evidence packages within agreed timeframes, and to notify customers of regulator inquiries concerning their services where legally permitted. For EU financial entity customers, Echelon accepts the access, audit and inspection rights DORA requires in ICT contracts. Evidence packages are generated per tenant so one customer's examination never exposes another's data.
current_practice: Not established; Echelon has not been examined by any regulator.
intended_practice: Include examination and cooperation clauses in the customer agreement template; build tenant-scoped evidence export.
customer_statement: Echelon has not been examined by any regulator. It will contractually acknowledge regulator examination authority over services it performs for banks under the Bank Service Company Act and commit to cooperate with customers' regulatory examinations.

challenge.customer_intent: Regulated customers must show examiners that outsourcing has not reduced the regulator's visibility.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An examiner cannot obtain information about an outsourced function, resulting in findings against the customer.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Examination clauses establish rights but examiners rarely visit small vendors; in practice the customer requests documents on short deadlines, and vendors without ready evidence fail those requests.
challenge.legally_required: For services to insured depository institutions, 12 U.S.C. 1867(c) subjects the services to examination by statute regardless of contract. Most DAF sponsors are charities, not banks, so BSCA applies only when a bank or bank-affiliated customer is served.
challenge.contractually_required: Standard in bank vendor contracts; DORA mandates access rights for EU financial entities.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not eliminable; it is a legal right. The burden of response can be reduced.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Evidence produced continuously so examination requests are answered from existing records.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Standing, tenant-scoped evidence packages that customers can hand to examiners, plus the contractual acknowledgment.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Customers can request a sample package at any time.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely; examiners value timely, complete records.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Examiners may still require on-site or direct access.
challenge.alternative_risks: Pre-packaged evidence may be seen as curated; it must be reproducible from source records.
supporting_arguments: Same evidence serves SOC and examination purposes.
opposing_arguments: Small vendor capacity during simultaneous exams.

title: Sanctions exposure of Echelon itself
status_rationale: No record of screening Echelon's owners, personnel, contractors, vendors or customers against sanctions lists was located, and ownership details of Echelon Foundry, LLC are not established in the records reviewed. OFAC prohibitions apply to Echelon as a US person independent of any customer obligation.
target_answer: Echelon screens its owners, managers, personnel, contractors, vendors and customers against OFAC lists (including the 50 percent rule for ownership) at onboarding and on list changes, records results, and does not operate in or support customers in comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions without a license. Echelon provides customers an annual written attestation of its sanctions status and discloses any OFAC enforcement action or voluntary self-disclosure.
intended_practice: Perform and record initial screening of owners, personnel and vendors; adopt a short sanctions compliance procedure based on the OFAC framework.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet documented sanctions screening of its owners, personnel, vendors and customers. It plans to complete and record that screening and provide an attestation on request.
open_questions: Ownership and control structure of Echelon Foundry, LLC for 50 percent rule analysis.

title: Complaints handling and reporting to customers
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-SVC-005 requires classifying any expression of dissatisfaction as a complaint case with acknowledgment (default 2 business days), response targets (default 15 business days), taxonomy and escalation; UNB-GAP-026 and UNB-CHAR-027 address complaint escalation and charity complaints. CNV-PLT-005 includes correction alerts. Not implemented.
target_answer: Complaints from customers and from their donors, advisors and grantees are captured from every channel as complaint cases with acknowledgment and response deadlines, a taxonomy that flags potential regulatory issues (privacy, discrimination, misrepresentation, sanctions holds), root cause analysis and routing to the sponsor where the sponsor owns the decision. Customers receive complaint data and trend reports for their own complaint management and examinations. Echelon's own complaints about its service are tracked the same way.
intended_practice: Implement the complaint case profile per UNB-XIN-SVC-005.
customer_statement: Echelon's design includes complaint capture from all channels with acknowledgment and response deadlines, root cause analysis and reporting to customers. Not yet implemented.

title: Regulatory change management
status_rationale: UNB-RCN-REG-001 requires a regulatory-change watch list (including proposed section 4966 regulations, OFAC rule changes and state charitable solicitation changes) linked to affected requirements, with a status change opening an impact review within 10 business days. CNV-GRT-008 requires proposed regulations to be tracked as proposed, not effective. CNV-GOV-005 requires versioned, effective-dated policy packs with sponsor adoption. Not implemented.
target_answer: Echelon monitors primary sources for changes to laws and guidance in its register, records each item with status (proposed, final, effective) and the requirements and controls it affects, opens an impact review within a set period, and delivers changes as versioned, effective-dated policy packs that sponsors adopt affirmatively. Proposed rules are never applied as binding. Interpretations embedded in product rules require counsel approval; AI may summarize changes but not decide their effect.
customer_statement: Echelon plans a regulatory change watch list linked to affected requirements, with counsel-approved interpretations delivered as effective-dated policy updates. Not yet operating.

title: Support for customers' regulatory notification, reporting and recordkeeping obligations
status_rationale: Incident response requirements (SOC2-026) and OFAC report data generation (CNV-GRT-006, UNB-RCN-REG-003), Schedule D data (CNV-FIN-009) and retention rules (CNV-PLT-004, CNV-PLT-009) are specified. No incident notification commitments to customers exist and no production system exists.
target_answer: Echelon commits to notify each bank customer's designated contact as soon as possible when a computer-security incident has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services for four or more hours, consistent with the 2021 bank service provider rule; to notify covered broker-dealer and adviser customers of breaches of their customer information as soon as possible and within 72 hours, consistent with amended Regulation S-P service provider requirements; and to meet any shorter contractual deadlines. The platform produces data for customers' regulatory reports (OFAC blocked and rejected transaction reports, Form 990 Schedule D) and retains records in forms that meet customers' recordkeeping rules where those apply.
intended_practice: Add notification commitments to the customer agreement and incident runbooks; implement report data generation per the cited requirements.
customer_statement: Echelon plans to commit to regulatory-grade incident notification for bank and securities customers and to produce data for their regulatory reports. Not yet in place.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon incident response owner)
residual_risks: Records retained for securities recordkeeping rules may need specific storage attributes that must be confirmed with each customer's compliance function.
